findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical XOR plus Kernighan population-count solution: XOR isolates precisely the differing positions and each difference &= difference - 1 step removes one set bit. It is minimal, clear, conventional, and expert interview quality, so no inert candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 461 and its two-integer Python contract. The O(log max(x, y)) upper bound and O(1) space claim match at most one iteration per relevant bit and two scalar values; under the stated 31-bit nonnegative domain the work is also strictly bounded.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2064943582. Its XOR initialization, zero counter, positive-difference loop, lowest-set-bit clearing expression, counter increment, and return are identical to the protected app-local algorithm and data flow; only the LeetCode class wrapper differs.

The dense-bit widths 4, 16, and 31 stay inside the source's 31-bit domain and span 7.75x, forcing one protected iteration per differing bit. The current source passed all 7 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.04x the reference runtime. A correct control that rebuilds each successive mask from bit zero passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 4.68x.

The Approach exactly describes the protected XOR value, the lowest-set-bit clearing identity, termination over implicit leading zeros, the differing-bit iteration count, and constant storage. Its built-in, shifting, string, and repeated-mask alternatives and equal, zero, and highest-bit boundaries are accurate.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It preserves the Hamming-distance definition, both exact source examples, the four-bit first-example comparison and two differing positions, the sole combined input constraint, and the post-constraints note equating the task with problem 2220. The unsupported legacy third example was removed.
